dedupe_keys.name: review of open call record datasets concerning the us 911 emergency response system code for america reimagine 911

description: This workbook is a guide to where US cities publish open data about their 911 calls, so that researchers and journalists can find records of emergency calls and responses. The producer is the Reimagine 911 National Action Team of Code for America, a civic technology non-profit, whose volunteers searched in early 2021 for 911 and calls-for-service data in the 100 largest US cities, every state capital and the 82 cities with Code for America volunteer brigades. Coverage is those priority cities; each row describes a dataset found, with the publisher and a link to where it is available, and a codebook defines the fields. The workbook does not contain the call records themselves, which often run to millions of rows. It is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with a related online knowledge base. Caveats: a 2021 snapshot, so some links will have moved, many datasets cover police calls, not fire or ambulance, and field definitions differ between cities. Simulation uses: locating call-level data to calibrate demand for emergency service and dispatch models in US cities. Related records: the New York City 911 end-to-end response times (data-nyc-911-end-to-end-response-times), San Francisco fire and EMS calls (data-sf-fire-ems-calls-for-service) and the FCC 911 PSAP registry (data-fcc-911-master-psap-registry).
